slides.title: Routing strategy: partner with RouteSprout now, and buy only on conditional terms

paragraphs.text: ATLAS FIELDOPS · BOARD OF DIRECTORS · MARCH 2027 MEETING
Routing strategy: partner with RouteSprout now, and buy only on conditional terms
Should Atlas buy RouteSprout in 2027, and on what terms, rather than build or partner?
Board pre-read · prepared November 2026
All figures are from the briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data) or are labelled team assumptions. $ in millions unless stated.

slides.title: Do not buy RouteSprout on the proposed terms in 2027. Partner now, and keep a conditional option to buy later at no more than $8.5M upfront

paragraphs.text: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Do not buy RouteSprout on the proposed terms in 2027. Partner now, and keep a conditional option to buy later at no more than $8.5M upfront

Recommendation: Reject the $18.0M all-cash deal (Path A) and the staged deal as structured (Path B). Sign a two-year RouteSprout routing partnership ($1.2M minimum, live summer 2027) that includes a right of first refusal and a pre-agreed conditional purchase option. Exercise it at a Q1 2028 gate only if six evidence thresholds are met.
1  Cash
Neither acquisition path stays inside the cash limits.

Path A needs $22.0M against a $15.0M ceiling. Path B fits at signing ($14.5M), but 18 months of operating drag takes cash to $7.2–8.2M, below the $9.0M floor. Nothing in the plan funds the $7.0M earnout due in 2029.
2  Value
The value case is overstated, and payback takes more than 15 years.

$18.0M is 3.75x recognised ARR, not the sellers' 2.5x of bookings. The $2.4M cross-sell is ARR, not EBITDA. After margin, support and RouteSprout's losses it adds about $0.1M a year, and loses $1.2M a year in the low case.
3  Risk
Customer and execution risk is high and not priced in.
Logo churn rose from 12% to 21%, and 58% of ARR sits in 41 accounts. The sellers assume 100% renewal. 30% of the integration is unscoped, and the synergy evidence is correlation only.
4  Options
Only the partnership passes all four board criteria in 2027.

At most $1.2M is at risk, it is live this summer, and no customers have to migrate. It earns more than ownership at any routing ARR below about $3.5M. Building is affordable but ships no earlier than late 2028.
5  Terms
Buying stays possible, but only on conditional terms.

At most $8.5M upfront (about 1.8x verified ARR) and up to $9.5M more if earned, paid only while cash stays above the floor. Integrate through the API first, and keep RouteSprout's interface until its large accounts renew.
Source: Atlas FieldOps briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data); team analysis.

slides.title: Our starting hypothesis was to buy RouteSprout in 2027 on staged terms. It fails four of the five tests it has to pass, and the fifth is unproven

paragraphs.text: APPROACH: HYPOTHESIS-DRIVEN
Our starting hypothesis was to buy RouteSprout in 2027 on staged terms. It fails four of the five tests it has to pass, and the fifth is unproven
Initial hypothesis: Atlas should buy RouteSprout in 2027, using the staged structure (Path B, $11.0M upfront) to fit the $15.0M cash ceiling, because it is the fastest way to own routing.

data: What would have to be true
1. Affordable: cash stays at or above the $9.0M floor through 2028, and the earnout can be funded
Path B leaves $0.5M headroom at signing and falls to $7.2–8.2M by end-2028. The $7.0M earnout has no funding source.
2. Fairly priced: the price rests on verified recurring revenue
3.75x recognised ARR, not 2.5x. Bookings include multi-year contract value and pilots. No quality-of-earnings (QoE) review has been done.
3. Pays back: positive incremental contribution within a reasonable horizon
Run-rate contribution is +$0.07M (base) or −$1.21M (low) while integration support runs. Payback takes more than 15 years.
4. Protects customers: RouteSprout and Atlas renewals and 99.7% uptime survive integration
Churn rose from 12% to 21%. The case assumes 100% renewal. Replacing the interface before renewals risks churn. No cohort data exists.
5. Beats the alternatives on cash, payback, continuity and execution
The partnership earns more below about $3.5M of routing ARR and risks at most $1.2M. Building is slower but cheaper.

slides.title: On recognised ARR the $18.0M price is 3.75x revenue, 50% higher than the sellers' 2.5x, and even the $4.8M ARR figure has not been verified

paragraphs.text: 2 · VALUE AND PAYBACK
On recognised ARR the $18.0M price is 3.75x revenue, 50% higher than the sellers' 2.5x, and even the $4.8M ARR figure has not been verified
Price ÷ revenue measure, multiple (x)
Why $7.2M of bookings is the wrong denominator
•  It is not recurring revenue. The audit notes say the $7.2M includes multi-year contract value and one-time pilots. It is not a current recurring revenue rate.
•  Pilots are counted as if they renew. The sellers make no adjustment for one-year pilots that will not renew, so bookings overstate both value and retention-adjusted revenue.
•  Atlas policy is to value on recognised ARR. Corporate finance values recurring revenue on ARR ($4.8M), which gives 3.75x.
•  Even $4.8M is unverified. There is no QoE review and no independently verified ARR schedule. The 42% growth figure stops before the last quarter.
•  There are no earnings to support the price. EBITDA is −$1.0M, including founder salaries, so the price relies entirely on revenue quality and on synergies.
Path B's total, including the full earnout, is also $18.0M, which is 3.75x ARR. The structure moves when the money is paid, not how much is paid.
Source: Atlas FieldOps briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data); team analysis.

slides.title: RouteSprout's customers are churning faster and its revenue is concentrated, yet the sellers' case assumes every account renews

paragraphs.text: 3 · CUSTOMER CONTINUITY AND EXECUTION
RouteSprout's customers are churning faster and its revenue is concentrated, yet the sellers' case assumes every account renews
Annual customer logo churn, %
FY2026 ARR by account group, $M
Implications
•  Churn is rising: 21% of logos, against 12% two years earlier. About $1.0M of ARR is at risk each year.
•  Concentration magnifies the risk: losing a handful of the 41 large accounts would wipe out a year of cross-sell.
•  People drive renewals, not features: customer success interviews found account managers drive renewal decisions, so RouteSprout's account managers matter as much as its code.
•  Interface timing matters: the product VP warns that replacing RouteSprout's interface before large customers renew could add churn.
•  No cohort data: we cannot yet tell whether churn sits in small or large accounts. That is the first diligence item.
The sellers' case assumes 100% renewal of all 310 accounts, which is 0% churn.
58% vs 42% of $4.8M ARR. That is about $68K per large account against about $7.5K per other account.
Source: Atlas FieldOps briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data); team analysis.

slides.title: The synergy, retention and integration claims rest on correlations and untested plans, not on evidence of cause

paragraphs.text: 3 · CUSTOMER CONTINUITY AND EXECUTION
The synergy, retention and integration claims rest on correlations and untested plans, not on evidence of cause

data: "Customers who use routing renew at 95%, so routing causes retention"
Routing users are mostly larger, multi-branch firms with dedicated customer success teams. Smaller non-users renew at 78%. The feature effect is not isolated.
We credit no retention uplift to Atlas's core base, and we keep RouteSprout's account managers.
"Integration works when the product is under one general manager"
The cited companies were on average twice as large, with lower churn. The link between integration spend and cross-sell is a correlation with no causal identification.
Not transferable. We do not underwrite the $2.4M cross-sell. Earnouts carry that risk instead.
30% of the work is unscoped and the plan assumes zero change-management delay. API plus single sign-on (SSO) is simpler than migrating records and support.
Integrate through the API first. Scope 100% of the work and price the contingency before signing.
"2.5x recurring revenue" and $7.2M of "annual recurring new sales"
The $7.2M includes multi-year contract value and one-time pilots. It is unsuitable for valuation or for projecting retention.
Value on QoE-verified recognised ARR only.
A substantial part of the value depends on keeping key engineers for at least two years. No agreements are in place.
Signed 24-month retention agreements become a condition of the deal.
